Draft sampling dtype mismatch\nlogits_to_probs\ncomputes the draft distribution as:\np\n=\nsoftmax\n(\nlogits\n.\nfloat\n()\n/\nT\n)\nand uses that float32\np\nin the speculative acceptance ratio\nmin(1, q / p)\nand correction distribution. In effect, the draft token was drawn from a represented distribution\nr\n, but acceptance and correction were computed as if it came from\np\n.\nFor a one-token speculative step, with sample distribution\nr\nbut acceptance math using\np\n:\na_y = min(1, q_y / p_y)\nc_y = (q_y - p_y)_+ / sum_z (q_z - p_z)_+\nPr[out = y] = r_y a_y + (sum_x r_x (1 - a_x)) c_y\nWhen\nr = p\n, this collapses to the target distribution\nq\n. A replica-deterministic sample sets a value\n  threshold and a 256-bin scale; every CTA walks its slice once; the last-arriving CTA merges\n  the bin-major publish tables and resolves the crossing bin with an exact key-space select.\n  Rows up to 16K columns never enter that pipeline: a census arm (<= 4K) and a register-resident\n  arm (4K to 16K) solve them in one CTA. Floods past the tie capacity are refined from the\n  crossing bin's exact key range; anything else falls through to a fused exact re-solve on\n  device, so every call stays sync-free and CUDA-graph capturable.\n- `radix_primitives` \u2014 SGLang's coarse-histogram structure made exact (no tie truncation),\n  fp32/fp16/bf16, grouped rows (`next_n`) and compressed columns (`compress_ratio`), optional\n  values, multi-CTA long rows.\n- `cutlass_primitives` \u2014 the vendored cutlass-primitives library (`VENDORED.md`, Apache-2.0):\n  register, clustered-register and streaming kernels with a census split for large k; the\n  full-row leader. `flashinfer.topk_varlen` exports its workspace helpers\n  (`cutlass_primitives_workspace_bytes`, `cutlass_primitives_row_order`) and\n  `release_cutlass_primitives_resources`.\n- `sglang` \u2014 SGLang's own DeepSeek-V4 indexer top-k (Apache-2.0, vendored verbatim from upstream\n  commit 7f27bf4708; `csrc/sglang_dsv4/VENDORED.md`, `licenses/LICENSE.sglang.txt`) under the\n  same contract, including a paged variant: the same kernel SGLang runs, for parity and for the\n  check that the FlashInfer API adds no overhead over the raw kernel. It is exact only while the\n  rank-k bin holds at most 2048 candidates, so `auto` never selects it.\n\n**Fused paged output.** `top_k_varlen(..., page_table=table, page_size=64)` returns physical\nKV slots `page_table[q, c // page_size] * page_size + c % page_size` from the selection launch\nitself (the SGLang DSA decode contract, one kernel instead of a top-k plus a transform pass).\nThe table is a contiguous, 16-byte-aligned int32 `(requests, max_pages)` tensor covering every\nrequest's valid length; it may be narrower than the logits width, and rows past its coverage\nare clamped to the covered prefix. Served by `walkfirst_primitives`, `radix_primitives` and\n`sglang`; `backend=\"auto\"` with a page table ranks the two exact primitives backends (they are\noutside the unpaged ranking).\n\n**Also in this PR:** a fix to the pre-existing multi-CTA `radix` kernel (chunks shorter than\ntheir misaligned prefix read past the valid length and wrote shared memory at negative offsets;\nCTA 0 could reset the group's arrival counter while a time-sliced peer still spun on it; the\nper-group state grows by one int, STATE_SIZE 770 to 771, allocated internally with a bumped\ncache key), the trace template for `top_k_varlen` extended with the paged inputs (the page size\nnames the paged definitions), the benchmarks that produced the numbers below, the four new\nbackends in `benchmarks/routines/topk_varlen.py`, and a one-line fix to\n`tests/trace/example.py` (an upstream call passed a `str` device to `is_sm100a_supported`, which\ncrashes the example on sm_100 hosts).\n\n**Why.** The DSA indexer runs one top-k per layer per decode step; SGLang today uses its own\nfused kernel. These backends are exact where that kernel approximates, faster on every decode\ncell we measured across six architectures, and fuse the page-table output so an engine needs\none launch. "https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/60559", "title": "[RFC]: TPSP Fusion Design", "body": "### Motivation.\n\n# RFC: TPSP Fusion Design\n\n## 0. Goal\n\nTPSP decomposes AllReduce into ReduceScatter (RS) + AllGather (AG), fusing RS/AG with adjacent compute (Norm, routing, GEMM) to hide communication behind computation. This brings roughly **10% TTFT improvement on long prefills**, which is especially valuable for today's agentic workloads where long-context prefill is common.\n\n\n## 1. TPSP Design Principles\n\n- **Conditionally enable TPSP based on measured performance:** A model may be compatible with TPSP without benefiting from it. Auto-profiling should identify the workload-specific crossover point, disable TPSP below it where overhead outweighs the gains, and enable it above it.\n- **Enable TPSP model by model:** TPSP changes model execution structure, so models should opt in individually until the approach is sufficiently established. Models not enabled for TPSP should continue using the existing path, with no TPSP-induced change in behavior or performance.\n- **Require device-side kernel support:** TPSP relies on fused kernels that may be model- and device-specific. If the required kernel is unavailable on a device, TPSP should automatically be disabled and the existing path used.\n- **Share the auto-profiling framework while allowing platform-specific tuning:** Provide common profiling logic that platforms can override or extend to account for their hardware characteristics. The profiling process should complete in about 60 seconds.\n\n---\n\n## 2. Dense Architecture\n\nTwo fusion sites per decoder layer: **o_proj** (after attention) and **down_proj** (after MLP).\n\n**Site A \u2014 o_proj \u2192 RS \u2192 Norm \u2192 AG**\n```\n the move from full-graph `torch.compile` to manual fusion expressed directly in model code. This issue tracks the concrete porting work for **section 1-1** of that RFC: enumerating the fusions currently performed by `vllm/compilation/passes/` and mapping each one to a work item to port to a manual call site in model code. To be clear this workstream is meant to touch all existing portable model definitions where compiler fusion pass would apply previously.\n\nThe goal is **no performance regression** as we delete each compiler pass. Each fusion below is either:\n- ported to a \"big fused op\" callable from model code,\n- collapsed into another fused op,\n- or explicitly dropped (with rationale).\n\n## Proposed Change.\n\n### Changes to QuantMethod\n\nThis is clearly needed for fusions where we are fusing the input quant op from a downstream Linear layer. When a linear layer ops in, by registering a `self.input_quant_key = QuantKey.XX`, the fused operation will return a new `QuantizedActivation` instead of a `torch.Tensor`. When the linear's kernel sees that the input is not a simple unquantized tensor, it will pass it through directly to the matmul without requantizing.\n\nFor an illustrative example for `RMSNorm + Quant` see https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/42469\n\n### Changes to Attention\n\nTBD\n\n### Changes to model definitions\n\nWe will initially implement these fusions for the simplest models that we can start with, and produce several subsequent PRs where we migrate groups of models to use these manual fusions, carefully testing performance and accuracy for at least one model within an architecture.\n\n### Inventory of fusion passes\n\nIn rough priority order. "rank": -9.93969082461554}, {"id": "github:vllm-project/vllm:60326", "source": "github", "kind": "pr", "url": "https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60326", "title": "[Bugfix] Enable MLA RoPE+KV-cache fusion when layer names are hoisted", "body": "## Overview\n\nFixes #60325.\n\nDefault `-O2` enables the existing MLA RoPE + KV-cache fusion for CUDA/ROCm MLA models when the attention layer name is a hoisted `LayerName`. The pass was off because `unified_mla_kv_cache_update` is still a Dynamo splitting op.\n\n## Claims\n\n- DeepSeek-V2/V3-style MLA at default `-O2` leaves `vllm::unified_mla_kv_cache_update` in the compiled piece, so `MLARoPEKVCacheCatFusionPass` can match.\n- Non-MLA models and a model-less `VllmConfig()` keep today's splitting ops.\n- `VLLM_USE_LAYERNAME=0`, torch older than 2.11, and platforms other than CUDA/ROCm keep the flag off.\n- An explicit `fuse_rope_kvcache_cat_mla=True` that still splits the op out is disabled, with a warning.\n- HiSparse with Inductor graph partition off keeps the op eager, including when HiSparseConnector turns HiSparse on after the `-O2` default.\n- `use_inductor_graph_partition` stays off by default. `splitting_ops_contain_kv_cache_update()` is unchanged, so the AITER RoPE+KV default does not flip on.\n\n## Validation\n\nConfig decisions are covered in `tests/compile/test_config.py`:\n\n- `test_mla_rope_kvcache_fusion_splitting`: MLA + LayerName, non-MLA, plain string names, non-CUDA, no model, explicit enable with and without LayerName.\n- `test_mla_fusion_follows_inductor_graph_partition`: partition on still enables the flag with no model.\n- `test_mla_fusion_disabled_when_user_splits_the_op`: a user `splitting_ops` list that still contains the MLA cache op.\n- `test_mla_fusion_stays_split_for_hisparse`: HiSparse set before the default, and the late HiSparseConnector case.\n\n`ruff check` and `ruff format --check` passed on the three files with ruff 0.14.10.\n\nThe new tests were not executed in this environment. Current main does not import on the local torch 2.5.1 (`torch._inductor.custom_graph_pass` and `torch.float8_e8m0fnu` are absent; main pins torch 2.13.0).\n\nNot run, and they need a GPU:\n\n- `tests/compile/passes/test_mla_rope_kvcache_cat_fusion.py`\n- `tests/kernels/core/test_rotary_embedding_mla_cache_fused.py`\n- a DeepSeek-V2/V3 compile under default piecewise CUDA graphs, to confirm the pass matches and the cache write replays\n\n## Details\n\n`-O2` applies `enable_rope_kvcache_mla_fusion` before `set_splitting_ops_for_v1`. With graph partition off and `splitting_ops is None`, `splitting_ops_contain_kv_cache_update()` returns true because #33267 will append both cache-update ops. The flag stays false, and the MLA op is then split out. The fusion pattern is RoPE and that op in one piece, so it cannot match.\n\nOn torch >= 2.11, `LayerName` is a hoisted graph input, so that string constant is gone. The new branch returns true only for an MLA model on CUDA or ROCm, and `set_splitting_ops_for_v1` then skips appending `vllm::unified_mla_kv_cache_update`. `vllm::unified_kv_cache_update` is still appended.\n\nIf the pattern matches, the piece contains `fused_rope_unified_mla_kv_cache_update`. If it does not, the unfused op is still inside the piecewise CUDA graph. `use_inductor_graph_partition=True` already does that: fusion runs on the full graph, then `maybe_use_cudagraph_partition_wrapper` wraps each partition. The op reads `slot_mapping` from `BlockTable.slot_mapping.gpu`, which is filled in place before replay. That replay was not checked on a GPU here.\n\nHiSparse's `prepare_kv_cache_update` has to run from Python every step, so the op stays a splitting op when partition is off.\n\n`use_mla` is also true for DeepSeek-V4. SM89 implements the instruction `mma.sync.aligned.m16n8k32.row.col.f32.e4m3.e4m3.f32` (`QMMA.16832.F32.E4M3.E4M3`). It does not have the SM90 features (no TMA, no `mbarrier.try_wait.parity`, no WGMMA, no clusters). It could not reuse the SM90 or SM100 kernels. It fell back to BF16 through cuBLASLt.\n- FP8 users on Ada had to dequantize and run BF16. They lost about 2\u00d7 of Tensor Core throughput.\n- The shared SM80/SM89 path also gave wrong error messages. An SM89 user saw a message that did not apply to their GPU.\n\n## Design\n\nSM89 has no TMA and no asynchronous barriers. The kernel uses the pre-Hopper primitives.\n\n- It uses `mma.sync` (wrapped in `deep_gemm/mma/sm89.cuh`, with A/B/C fragment layouts documented) and `ldmatrix.x4` for operand staging.\n- It uses a multi-stage `cp.async` pipeline with a 128-byte XOR swizzle.\n- It uses a persistent block scheduler (one CTA per SM). Tiles walk in a loop.\n- It uses direct global stores because SM89 has no TMA store. It has an alignment-safe scalar tail. An MMA lane owns a pair of adjacent columns. For odd N the element offset of a row can be odd. A 2-element vector store is then illegal. This caused the original misaligned address failure.\n- Block K is fixed at 128 because of the per-128-channel scaling granularity. Pipeline depth and tile shapes come from a new cost model in `csrc/jit_kernels/heuristics/sm89.hpp`. The warp split uses one shared function `get_mma_sync_warps_n()`. Host heuristics and device code both call it so they cannot disagree.\n\nBoth SM90 SF recipes are supported:  \n`(1, 1, 128)` (per-token A and B scales) and  \n`(1, 128, 128)` (per-token A, one B scale per 128-column N block).  \nThe second recipe is the default when FP32 scales are used. SM89 uses the same FP32 SF layouts as SM90. The function `transform_sf_into_required_layout` was extended. It was not duplicated.\n\n## Scope\n\nSupported features:  \ndense FP8 GEMM, K-major (NT) operands only, FP32 and BF16 outputs, `D = C + A @ B`, ragged M/N, `k % 16 == 0`, both aliases (`fp8_fp4_gemm_nt`, `fp8_gemm_nt`, `fp4_gemm_nt`), and shape specialization.\n\nStill rejected (with an explicit message that names the requirement):  \ngrouped and K-grouped FP8, MN-major FP8 operands, FP4, custom epilogues, `alpha` scaling, PDL, and MQA/attention.  \nBF16 keeps its cuBLASLt fallback.\n\n## Incidental fixes\n\n- `set_pdl()` now panics below SM90. It no longer sets a flag that `griddepcontrol` cannot honour.  \n  `cudaGridDependencySynchronize()` is wrapped in a no-op below `__CUDA_ARCH__ >= 900` so the SF-layout kernels compile for SM89.\n- `call_cublaslt_api` used `CUBLAS_COMPUTE_32F_FAST_TF32` for non-FP32 operands. That mode only down-casts FP32 inputs to TF32. BF16/FP8 operands ran at TF32 precision by mistake. Now only FP32 inputs use that mode.\n- A new `DG_PANIC` macro throws always and carries a message.\n\n## Bug found during validation\n\nThe persistent loop primed its `cp.async` pipeline only in the prologue before the tile loop. It relied on a cross-tile tail load to prime the next tile. A tile\u2019s tail can only reach the stages that are already free of the current tile \u2014 prologue stages `p \u2208 [0, kNumStages-2-num_k_blocks]`. The next tile\u2019s K loop consumes `p = 0..num_k_blocks-1`. When `num_k_blocks < kNumStages-1` (example: `k=512`, 4 blocks, 8 stages) the high stages were never reloaded. The next tile read the previous tile\u2019s shared memory. Symptom: non-deterministic `nan` and values near 1e30. The problem appeared only for small M spread over many N tiles.\n\nThe fix extracts the prologue into `prime_pipeline()` and re-primes unconditionally after the epilogue. The re-prime is guarded by `cp_async_wait<0>()` and a `__syncthreads()`. `cp.async` completion is per-thread, so both are required before the stages can be reused. The change removes a prologue/epilogue overlap that was never correct. Measured cost is about 0\u20133.5 % (4096\u00b3: 2518 \u00b5s vs 2507 \u00b5s, within noise; 4096\u00d74096\u00d7512: 420 \u00b5s vs 405 \u00b5s).\n\n`tests/test_sm89.py` added the shapes `(1, 4096, 512)`, `(64, 4096, 512)` and `(128, 4096, 128)`. Reverting the fix makes these tests fail (34 failures). They are real regression tests.\n\n## Testing\n\nHardware: RTX 4060 Laptop (SM89, 24 SMs, 7.6 GiB), CUDA 13.0, PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130.\n\n- `tests/test_sm89.py` \u2014 17 tests, OK from a cold JIT cache (~130 s).  \n  Covers both recipes \u00d7 both output dtypes \u00d7 accumulate \u00d7 12 shapes, explicit `recipe=(1,128,128)`, `recipe_a`/`recipe_b` pairs, entry-point aliases, c", "created_at": "2026-10-14T19:01:11Z", "updated_at": "2026-10-16T18:30:02Z", "fetched_at": "2026-10-20T12:14:23Z", "state": "open", "merged_at": null, "parent": null, "tags": ["h100", "throughput", "performance", "nvfp4"], "metadata": {"number": 474, "labels": [], "comments": 0, "state_reason": null}, "content_hash": "e9e726ee03fe75aa494d2982073d7cff644a759f6b2dc7cbce2a25919d9f2557", "rank": -7.828445969186708}, {"id": "github:deepseek-ai/DeepGEMM:406", "source": "github", "kind": "pr", "url": "https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepGEMM/pull/406", "title": "Add SM120 heuristic calibration harness", "body": "## Summary\n\nAdds an SM120 GEMM heuristic calibration script on `nv_dev`, addressing #385. Neither needs new cubins; both are arch-neutral except where noted. (The CuTe-DSL per-call scale kernel, originally part 3 of this PR, is now #6800.)\n\n### 1. Autotuner: `auto` picks the fastest cached runner, and re-races runners it has never measured\n\n`AutoTuner.search_cache` walked the runner list in order and returned the first runner that had a cached winner. Once backends had been tuned individually (a harness run with several `--backends`, or a server that tunes `cublas` explicitly and later calls `auto`), `auto` resolved to whichever runner was listed first, not the fastest one: on Rubin tuned `auto` equalled tuned CUTLASS on 15/15 `bmm_fp8` shapes even though tuned cuBLAS was about 1.6x faster. In tuning mode the same lookup also treated a single cached runner as a hit for the whole bucket, so the other candidates were never profiled (CodeRabbit raised this on #6521).\n\nThe fix keeps every runner's best measured time next to its winner (`_winner_times`, keyed like the policy map by winner identity + cache key):\n\n- when a race profiles several runners, each runner's best `(time, tactic)` is recorded, not only the global winner's; a losing runner that already had an explicit winner entry is refreshed to the tactic just measured so its time and tactic agree;\n- `search_cache` ranks in-memory hits by that time and returns the fastest; entries without a time (legacy, promoted from the managed store, seeded by tests) rank last and still resolve by list order among themselves;\n- a tuning-mode lookup (`require_profiling_policy=True`) is a hit only if every candidate runner has either a winner or a recorded time for the bucket; otherwise it falls through and `choose_one` races the missing ones. Serving-mode lookups are unchanged in cost (one dict probe per runner).\n\nPersistence formats are untouched: the v1 config file and the managed v2 store still hold only the winner, so a reload behaves exactly as before (list order) until the first race in the new process records times. `rank_tactics` also records the winner's time so a later `choose_one` on the same runner stays a cache hit. `_discard_profile_cache` and `clear_cache` drop the times with the winners.\n\nTest change: `test_cache_hit_disagreement_reprofiles_together[partial_memory]` seeded rank 0 with a winner for runner A only and expected that to count as a hit over `[A, B]`. Under the new rule B is unmeasured, so rank 0 would (correctly) also miss and there would be no disagreement to test; the case now records a measured time for B as well, which restores the rank-0 hit / rank-1 miss setup the test is about. The final expectation (coordinated re-profile, `RunnerB` tactic 1 wins on both ranks) is unchanged.\n\n### 2. CUTLASS FP8 (SM100/103/107): shape-aware untuned tactic instead of always config 0\n\n`fp8_gemm_cutlass.cu` maps `tactic == -1` to `globalConfigs[0]` = 64x64x128 tile, 1x1x1 cluster, with a `// No heuristic for now` comment. Untuned, every CUTLASS `bmm_fp8` call therefore ran the smallest tile: at 512x8192x28672 that is 1024 CTAs each re-streaming K, 1.6-2.3x slower than cuBLAS on Rubin at m >= 512 and the reason `auto` looked so bad before #6521. The autotuner can already reach all 30 configs (6 tiles x 5 clusters), so the fix is only for the untuned default.\n\n`_cutlass_fp8_sm100_default_tactic(batch, m, n, num_sms)` picks, in `getConfigs()` enumeration order, the largest CTA tile whose CTA count still reaches the SM count, and always with the 1x1x1 cluster (the same cluster as today's default, so no new launch constraints). 128-row tiles are skipped when `m <= 64`. Weight-streaming shapes (m <= 64) keep config 0 exactly as before; large-M shapes move to 128x128 or 128x256. The selection is a pure function covered by a unit test; the C++ fallback is unchanged so explicit `tactic=-1` still works.\n\n### 3. CuTe-DSL `bmm_fp8` scale fusion\n\nMoved to its own PR, #6800, so it can merge independently.\n\n### Not in this PR\n\n- `mm_fp8` default routing and `bmm_fp8` runner order: #6521.\n- Small-M FP8 GEMM speed on Rubin itself: vendor kernels (cuBLAS two-kernel split-K, trtllm-gen low-latency cubins with 40 CTAs and no split-K); nothing in the library can close that gap.\n\n## \ud83d\udd0d Related Issues\n\nFollow-up to #6521. GEMM", "body": "## Summary\r\n\r\nThis PR tunes the `ll_bf16_gemm` router GEMM dispatch heuristic for critical models: GLM5.2, DSv3.2, DSv4-Flash, and DSv4-Pro on Hopper and Blackwell GPUs.\r\n\r\nRouter GEMM has shown up as an expensive kernel if it is not treated carefully. For the most critical models, we have historically used ad-hoc, PTX-based kernels focused on LL scenarios. However, those kernels are usually limited to a\r\nsingle shape, or to a very small set of shapes. Extending them to new models requires non-trivial kernel work, which is not ideal because each model family tends to bring its own router shape, and new shapes will keep appearing.\r\n\r\nPR [#42562](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/42562) introduced a generic cuteDSL implementation for this path. This PR is a follow-up that tunes the default configs and gets extra e2e performance on critical router shapes.\r\n\r\nIdeally, we should eventually add an autotuner that does this automatically for every router shape. That should be feasible, but PDL support in these kernels has shown (sometimes) non-deterministic behavior when comparing kernel-level and e2e benchmarks. A similar issue was discussed in [sglang#29470](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/29470): cold/warm cache kernel timings do not necessarily predict e2e behavior once PDL overlap enters the picture. In practice, different tuning configurations can change this, which makes it is difficult to infer from microbenchmarks how much overlap a PDL-launched router kernel will get, and thus e2e performance.\r\n\r\nBecause of that, this PR defines a small set of heuristics using e2e measurements after exhaustive token sweeps from 1 to 16.\r\n\r\n## What Changed\r\n\r\n- Adds architecture-specific tuning tables for SM100F and SM90.\r\n- Tunes dispatch for:\r\n  - `(4096, 256)` - DeepSeek-V4-Flash\r\n  - `(6144, 256)` - GLM5.2\r\n  - `(7168, 256)` - DeepSeek-V3.2\r\n  - `(7168, 384)` - DeepSeek-V4-Pro\r\n- Uses model-derived warmup shapes instead of a static model-shape list.\r\n\r\n## E2E Results\r\n\r\nSome highlighted results measured with the tuned dispatch configs. It splits the FP32 mixing weight into three BF16 components, accumulates their projections separately in FP32, and computes the input squared norm in the same pass.\n\nThis initial draft contains a kernel, correctness tests and a comparison benchmark. **Serving dispatch is intentionally not wired yet. No kernel or end-to-end speedup, numerical equivalence, or production-readiness claim is made.** Integration and default selection depend on real SM90 measurements against the current fused mHC path, not only against a standalone GEMM.\n\n## Implementation\n\n- Accept caller-owned prepared weights and output buffers; no allocation or CPU/GPU synchronization in the projection wrapper.\n- Write `[splits, tokens, mix]` projection and `[splits, tokens]` squared-norm partials, compatible with the existing prenorm epilogue layout.\n- Support split counts 1/4/16, token tiles 32/64/128, empty batches, masked tails, and contiguous offset views. These are tuning candidates, not validated performance defaults.\n- Reuse the existing mHC correctness suite. Add FP64 reference, cancellation/weight-reconstruction, output-boundary and changed-input/weight CUDA graph tests.\n- Add a CUPTI benchmark that checks correctness before timing and sweeps both DeepGEMM and candidate configurations with CUDA graphs and cold L2. Weight preparation, allocations and the common epilogue are excluded from the reported prenorm timing.\n\nThe prepared weights occupy 6 bytes per original FP32 element, in addition to any retained original weight. The caller must rebuild them after weight updates. Different accumulation orders can change outputs; batch invariance is not promised. SGLang's bundled serving gains are not an estimate for this isolated kernel or for vLLM.\n\n## Duplicate check and provenance\n\nChecked #57448 and public open/closed PR searches for `mHC`, `compensated`, `bf16x3`, `SM90`, and Hopper on 2026-10-09. No open PR implementing this compensated mHC projection was found.\n\n- #60768 only opts SM90 into the existing TF32 coefficient-overlap path; this is an independent kernel draft, not a duplicate or dependency.\n- #57603 implements small-batch overlap; #56633 fuses post/pre; #56962 integrates Mega-mHC. They are relevant baselines, not this BF16x3 projection.\n- #60376 is a router-GEMM optimization on SM100, not mHC prenorm on SM90.\n- #59129 concerns the separate DeepGEMM SM90 correctness fix and must be accounted for when benchmarking the baseline.\n\nThe SGLang kernel's Apache-2.0 attribution is retained. "https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/6621", "title": "refactor(moe_ep)!: move the MoE all-to-all ops out of flashinfer.comm into their moe_ep backends; retire backend=\"trtllm\" and the moe_comm bench; SM107 one-sided build fix", "body": "## \ud83d\udccc Description\n\nFollow-up to #6047. Now that `flashinfer.moe_ep` owns the MoE all-to-all backends, this removes what stayed behind in `flashinfer.comm` for the old paths, and fixes the NVLink one-sided module on GR100. After it, every `MoEEpCommunication` backend owns its kernels under `flashinfer/moe_ep/backends/split/comm/<backend>/` (as `nvlink_one_sided` already did), and `flashinfer/comm/` keeps no MoE all-to-all code. Five commits:\n\n### 1. `fix(moe_ep)`: native `sm_107a` for the NVLink one-sided module\n\n`gen_nvlink_one_sided_alltoall_module` (then `gen_moe_ep_nvlink_one_sided_module`) inherited the global JIT arch flags, which map SM107 to `sm_100f` while the bundled CUTLASS lacks `Sm107`. The driver rejects that code on GR100 (`Mercury Validator: Validation failed for SM 107`), so the first launch failed with `cudaErrorUnknown`. These kernels use no CUTLASS, so the module now passes `get_nvcc_flags_list()` and builds every target natively. The receiver then waits on hardware byte counters instead of per-round completion flags, and the CFT dispatch also fills the padding rows' expert ids itself. The logical endpoint is bound to the existing MNNVL workspace, so no extra memory is allocated.\n- **Up to 256 EP ranks** (was 64); the active-rank mask grows to four words.\n- **Workspace laid out by phase.** Round state, dispatch control and payload, and combine control, input and the CFT receive inbox are separate regions with fixed capacities, which every op validates.\n- **Routing and fan-out.**\n  - Invalid expert ids are skipped during routing.\n  - When `top_k > ep_size`, dispatch and combine fan out over a compact per-rank destination list.\n  - Receive counters are double-buffered by round parity; the CFT dispatch publishes them right after routing.\n- **Low-precision combine** pairs FP8 conversions.\n- **Timeouts** are chosen on the host per launch.\n\n### Python\n\n- `NVLinkOneSidedAlltoAll` drives the new JIT module (`moe_ep_nvlink_one_sided_alltoall`) directly.\n  - **Workspace sharing:** instances with the same layout share one workspace, which is freed when its last instance is destroyed. Instances on one workspace must run their rounds one after another; a dispatch while another instance's round awaits its combine raises.\n  - **CFT setup:** endpoint creation and exchange run over the EP group's `CommBackend`, so no MPI is involved. Every rank agrees on CFT before the layout is fixed, and a failure on any rank falls back to the fence path on all ranks.\n- `NVLinkOneSidedConfig` gains:\n  - `cft`: `None` uses CFT automatically where supported, for steps up to `cft_max_tokens_for_dispatch` / `cft_max_tokens_for_combine` tokens (128 each); `True` uses it on every supported step; `False` never uses it;\n  - `timeout_sec`: the bound on each wait for a peer;\n  - `enable_pdl`: programmatic dependent launch, `None` enabling it on SM90+ as before (also on `CakeAlltoAllConfig`).\n- `NVLinkOneSidedAlltoAll.active_rank_mask(ranks)` builds the 256-rank mask, and `cft_enabled` reports whether CFT is available to the instance.\n- **`CakeAlltoAll`** is now a standalone `MoEEpCommunication` (it used to subclass `NVLinkOneSidedAlltoAll`). NCCL's own `ncclGinBarrier` with `ncclGinAllContexts` exists for exactly this failure mode), and GIN signals are not ordered with NVLink stores from other threads (fixed upstream in deepseek-ai/DeepEP#715, not in `d4f41e4e`).\r\n- The receiver's copy epilogue (PDL-launched) can therefore read **stale raw-buffer rows from the previous dispatch**: phantom/missing expert routes, double-assigned slots, unwritten `recv_x` rows, occasionally OOB slots \u2014 the latter surfacing as the `combine_impl` illegal-memory-access crashes seen in DP=8 direct-mode nightlies.\r\n\r\nRoot-cause evidence (pristine DeepEP, host-side audit, zero kernel instrumentation): internal repro `repros/pr57991-waldorf-20260928/.../count-discrepancy-audit-20261002/REPORT.md`.\r\n\r\n## The patch\r\n\r\n`tools/ep_kernels/patches/deepep-gin-barrier-data-visibility.patch` \u2014 one file (`deep_ep/include/deep_ep/common/comm.cuh`), two changes mirroring shipped upstream fixes:\r\n\r\n1. **Per-context signals**: after the existing flush + grid sync, signal every peer on every GIN context (`ginContextCount \u00d7 kNumRanks` signals) and wait on the per-(context, signal id) slots. A signal posted on context `c` is SQ-FIFO-ordered behind all WQEs previously reserved on context `c`, covering the RDMA data puts. Mirrors NCCL's `ncclGinBarrierSession` with `ncclGinAllContexts` (`nccl_device/impl/gin_barrier__funcs.h`).\r\n2. **`fence.acq_rel.sys` for world-team barriers** before the barrier signal, so same-node peers' NVLink TMA stores are visible before the GIN signal is published. Mirrors upstream DeepEP #715 (11d1cab), which postdates our pinned commit.\r\n\r\nApplied in `install_python_libraries.sh` after the DeepEP clone, guarded to the pinned commit `d4f41e4e` (skips on any other ref) and idempotent (grep guard). `docker/Dockerfile` copies the new `tools/ep_kernels/patches` dir into the extensions-build stage.\r\n\r\n## Why this is not duplicating an existing PR\r\n\r\nNo vLLM PR touches the DeepEP barrier. GPU util \u224887% at 220 W of 600 W \u2192 **communication-bound on PCIe**, not compute-bound. ~7K tok/s looks like the ceiling for this board without NVLink.\n\nRadix/prefix cache is the only large multiplier: cache-hit prefill **0.34 s for a 112K-token prefix \u2248 325K tok/s (\u224839\u00d7)**.\n\nDecode (client path over SSH tunnel, production config): prose 93.9 tok/s, structured/JSON 134.1 tok/s, TTFT 143\u2013169 ms.\n\n## DSPARK A/B (block_size=2, clean legs, each verified via `server_info` + acceptance length)\n\n| Prompt class | DSPARK ON | DSPARK OFF |\n|---|---|---|\n| prose | 76.5\u201378.9 tok/s | 36.4\u201336.5 tok/s |\n| structured | 120.3\u2013120.5 tok/s | 36.5 tok/s |\n| `accept len` | 3.0 tokens/step | 1.0 |\n\nWith DSPARK off the model flattens to ~36.5 tok/s regardless of prompt class \u2014 speculation is the difference between usable and unusable latency on this hardware. Production ships `block_size=6` (structured \u2248237\u2013252 tok/s vs 120 at block 2).\n\n## Traps that cost us experiments (SGLang-specific)\n\n1. **`--enable-expert-parallel` is a vLLM flag** \u2014 SGLang takes `ep_size`; the vLLM spelling is rejected outright.\n2. **`docker run` must pass `TP_SIZE`/`DP_SIZE`/`EP_SIZE` explicitly.** Without `-e`, the container silently serves TP8 defaults and your \"new\" config never happens (we recorded a full sweep of false data this way before adding a config gate).\n3. **`ep_size \u2264 tp_size`** or the MoE rank computation divides by zero: `moe_ep_rank = tp_rank % (tp_size // moe_dp_size) // (tp_size // moe_dp_size // ep_size)`.\n4. **DSPARK + DP attention requires `--enable-dp-lm-head`** \u2014 but is unreachable on this model anyway (next section).\n\n## Topologies SGLang rejects on this model\n\n| Attempt | Result |\n|---|---|\n| DP2 \u00d7 TP4 (any EP) | `ValueError: V4.1 vision currently supports TP/EP without DP, CP, PP or MoE A2A` \u2014 both replicas die within ~70 s |\n| prefill context-parallel | same class of rejection |\n| `--enable-dp-attention` alone | silently no DP group (`dp_size: 1`) \u2014 looks fine, isn't |\n\nOther SM120 gaps we hit: MSCCL++ (`_tune` kernel crash), FlashInfer all-reduce fusion, `flashmla_sparse_q8`, and CUDA-graph capture for **prefill** (crashes even with DSPARK off, i.e. unrelated to speculation).\n\n## Operational notes\n\n- A defunct container can survive a single `docker rm -f`; the next `docker run` then fails on the name conflict while an orphaned engine process keeps the port and answers health checks \u2014 which silently mislabels the next experiment. Loop `docker rm -f` until the container is gone **and** nothing listens on the port.\n- A parse failure must never satisfy an \"expected config\" assertion, or a server that has not started yet gets "hf:2610.01380", "source": "huggingface", "kind": "paper", "url": "https://huggingface.co/papers/2610.01380", "title": "GPU-Initiated Communication: Dissecting Down to the Bone", "body": "GPU-initiated communication lets GPU threads post RDMA operations directly to the NIC. It underpins NVSHMEM, NCCL GIN, and DeepEP, which serve the fine-grained, latency-critical communication of Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models, yet its performance characteristics and optimizations remain scarcely documented beyond source code, and library comparisons fail to separate the costs of the hardware mechanism from those of the library around it.\n  This paper dissects GPU-initiated communication at the GPU-NIC boundary. We first detail the GPU-side network path: queue placement, work-request construction, doorbell ordering, and completion semantics. We then introduce mini-gda and mini-proxy, minimal transports for the GPU and CPU-proxy submission paths, and measure them alongside NVSHMEM IBGDA, NCCL GIN, DeepEP, UCCL-EP, MSCCL++, and fabric-lib on NVIDIA H100, H200, B200, and GB200 platforms. A minimal GPU path issues an operation in 0.7 \u03bcs and completes in 4.0 \u03bcs; libraries add up to 4.6 \u03bcs of issue time through queue management, memory ordering, and completion scope, and issue time scales with the SM clock. A tuned CPU proxy matches or beats the GPU path at idle, at the cost of a dedicated core whose operating state sets its latency and throughput. On either path, sharing a queue with bulk traffic raises latency by one to three orders of magnitude. Reaching the 260 M msg/s ceiling of our InfiniBand platform requires doorbell batching and queue parallelism, and both have resource costs: communication code can reduce GPU block residency even when unused, and all-to-all traffic loses 59% of its NIC message rate at about 3,000 active connections. The submission path alone therefore does not predict communication performance.
